analysis.title: GS Blekos - CPI Preview / AI & Inflation / BCP (up) / BNP / Industrials Barometers / LSE / CTP / US Digital Ads Preview
key_insights: GS forecasts September core CPI at +0.24% m/m versus +0.2% consensus, and +2.46% y/y versus +2.5% consensus. Headline CPI is forecast at +0.59% versus +0.6% consensus, driven by higher energy prices.
GS's September core CPI forecast is consistent with a slightly smaller +0.20% increase in core PCE for September.

GS estimates AI price pressures are boosting core PCE inflation by about 45bp now, roughly half of it a genuine effect and half mismeasurement. The effect is expected to peak at 50bp by end-2026 and fall to 10bp by end-2027. The impact on headline PCE is about 5-10bp higher.

GS expects the AI inflation impact to fade next year mainly because its sector analysts expect memory and computer prices to grow much more slowly. That lowers both genuine cost pressure and the mismeasurement in the software and accessories category.

GS upgrades Banco Comercial Portugues (BCP.LS) to Buy from Neutral after recent underperformance. It expects above-sector-average EPS growth and ROTE, supported by lending volume growth and lower legal provisions on CHF mortgages.
GS net profit estimates for BCP are about 5% above Visible Alpha consensus over 2027-28E, and GS sees scope for further consensus upgrades.

GS models BNP Paribas Q3'26 net profit (pre-AT1) of about €3.4bn, 3% above Visible Alpha consensus. Revenue is about €350mn (3%) above consensus, mainly from CIB and Retail. This is partly offset by a tax charge about €200mn above consensus (about 30% effective tax rate due to an exceptional item BNP guided to). Opex and provisions are broadly in line. BNP reports on 28 October.

GS Europe multi-industry 3Q26 barometers: the Global Barometer moved sideways but stays above its historical median. The US is above median, China has fallen below median, and Europe has improved but remains below median.

By end market, the barometers show the biggest upward moves in Electrical Equipment (Buy Prysmian, Nexans, Siemens, Rexel) and Marine (Buy Wartsila). General industrial, construction, tech and trucks improved slightly. Rail (Sell Alstom), A&D and Autos (Sell Sandvik, SKF) deteriorated, and consumer remains very weak.
London Stock Exchange Group confirmed discussions to acquire Octus.
CTP N.V. announced a €100mn share buyback programme.

GS US Digital Ads Q3'26 preview: investor debates on Alphabet and Meta center on AI-driven capex and capital intensity, potential funding needs, and positioning in the consumer agent landscape. GS sees both as having a right to win at the platform layer of AI-driven consumer behavior.

Investors are more comfortable with current-period ROIC on prior spending, supported by Google Cloud growth and Meta product innovation. Questions remain about the revenue and EBIT contribution needed in 2028-2030 to earn adequate returns on 2026/2027 capex.
